text:
Naomi Feldman: Kicking off thread on SIEM-ready audit export beta definition + success metrics + who we onboard first. Need input esp from CS/SE on which customers are “ready” + most painful use cases. We can support Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and S3 (initial). Feature flag allowlist per-tenant.

Naomi Feldman: Proposed beta definition (v0):
- Destinations: Splunk HEC + Datadog Logs + S3
- Delivery: at-least-once, with dedupe guidance (`event_id` + `occurred_at` + `tenant_id`)
- Filters: event_type + actor + workspace/tenant + environment; time window for replay is operator-only
- Console: create destination, test delivery, view health (last success, last error, backlog estimate)
Non-goals: broad SIEM catalog, custom field mappings, “exactly once”.

Talia Benson: +1. Can we also write down explicit exit criteria for beta -> GA planning? Otherwise we’ll argue forever. :slightly_smiling_face:

Naomi Feldman: Yep. Draft success metrics (open to edits):
1) Delivery reliability: >= 99.9% of events delivered within 5 min (p95) per destination when sink is healthy
2) Loss: < 0.01% confirmed drop rate (excluding destination misconfig/auth failures)
3) Operability: oncall can detect + mitigate within 15 min (dashboards + alerts + runbook)
4) Setup: a new customer can get to “first event delivered” in < 30 min using docs
5) Security: secrets stored encrypted, least-privilege guidance for S3, audit log includes config changes

Marcus Lin: From Security perspective, I’d like the “sink is healthy” clause to be explicitly defined. Otherwise people interpret 401/token rotation as “we dropped events”. We should define “exporter responsibilities” vs “customer endpoint responsibilities”.

Sean Gallagher: For SRE, we’ll need metrics defined at the right boundary. I’d suggest:
- exporter_delivery_success_rate (2xx/ack) per sink
- exporter_delivery_latency (event occurred -> accepted by sink)
- exporter_backlog_age (oldest event waiting)
Then success criteria can be in terms of those signals. Also: if Splunk has 5xx for 30 mins, we should degrade/pause without paging nonstop.

Chloe Martin: Console side: “setup < 30 min” is doable if we keep the flow tight. But we need to be realistic about Splunk HEC config friction. We should count “customer has token + endpoint ready” as pre-req.

Naomi Feldman: Good call. Rephrasing Setup metric: “Given valid destination credentials + endpoint, first event delivered in < 30 min” (docs + UI).

Olga Petrov: For compliance/evidence: we should log export destination CRUD as audit events themselves (who changed what, old/new). That’s part of beta success for SOC2 evidence trail. Also need a statement on PII/redaction (what fields can appear).

Naomi Feldman: Yes. Export config changes should generate AuditEvent v1 `audit.export.destination.*` events.

Talia Benson: On onboarding order: I want to ensure we pick 2–3 design partners that (a) will actually test, (b) cover the three sinks, and (c) cover Hosted + Dedicated + Private.

Naomi Feldman: Candidates I have from pipeline/CS notes:
- Northbridge Financial (Splunk, regulated)
- Echelon Health (Datadog)
- Altitude Defense (Private + S3/KMS, gov-adjacent)
- Stonewire Software (existing Dedicated, asked about roadmap)
CS/SE: who’s the best first 2 to avoid getting stuck on platform edge cases?

Colin O'Donnell: From SE side, I’d start with Echelon (Datadog) first. Datadog logs intake is usually the least “custom” and they move fast. Good for shaking out UI + basic connector semantics.

Colin O'Donnell: Northbridge is high value but they’ll come with a security questionnaire + strict expectations. I’d do them second, once we have (1) clear messaging on at-least-once duplicates and (2) the Splunk HEC ACK path stable.

Fatima Noor: Agree w/ Colin. Also Altitude (Private) will be heavy lift due to egress constraints + KMS + their change window. I’d not make them beta #1 unless we already have a Private install path mostly baked.

Priya Natarajan: Platform perspective: we can support Hosted/Dedicated easily in first iteration; Private has more packaging + networking unknowns. I’m ok with Private as “beta track B” but not the gating design partner for initial launch.

Naomi Feldman: Makes sense. Tentative sequencing:
1) Echelon Health (Datadog) — validate pipeline, filters, health UI
2) Northbridge Financial (Splunk) — validate ACK + throttling behavior + security review
3) Stonewire (Dedicated) — validate “scale” + noise filtering needs
4) Altitude (Private/S3) — validate installer + KMS + S3 partitioning

Sean Gallagher: If Stonewire has volume, I’d actually pull them earlier (maybe #2) because we’ll learn about backlog/backpressure sooner. Splunk 401/403 issues tend to be “people rotated token” not scaling.

Fatima Noor: Stonewire is already bought-in and can allocate eng time. They were specifically asking about admin/RBAC events, so they’ll be picky about event taxonomy. That’s useful early.

Marcus Lin: +1 on having at least one customer who will scrutinize “what events are included” early. That’s where we can accidentally oversell.

Naomi Feldman: Ok revised:
1) Echelon (Datadog)
2) Stonewire (Dedicated)
3) Northbridge (Splunk)
4) Altitude (Private/S3)

Talia Benson: What’s the beta “contract” / expectations? We should put it in writing for CS to send.

Naomi Feldman: Draft beta terms (internal):
- “Best effort” support, not covered by standard SLA
- At-least-once delivery; duplicates possible; customer responsible for dedupe using `event_id`
- Limited sinks (Splunk/Datadog/S3) and limited filters
- No full historical backfill; replay is by request/ops-assisted
- Feature may change; schema versioned (v1)

Olga Petrov: Please add data handling statement: exporter sends the AuditEvent schema fields, which may include IP address + user agent. No payload contents / prompts / model outputs included. (We should be crisp.)

Naomi Feldman: Added.

Chloe Martin: For success metric “< 5 min p95” — is that end-to-end or “accepted by sink”? Console health will be based on exporter’s view (accepted). If Splunk indexes slowly, that’s out of our control.

Sean Gallagher: Strongly recommend metric is “accepted by sink” + we expose “last_accepted_at” timestamp. Otherwise we’re debugging Splunk indexing pipelines.

Naomi Feldman: Agreed. Metric updated: “accepted by sink” p95 <= 5 min, assuming sink endpoints respond successfully.

Priya Natarajan: One more: we should define “beta start” as “feature flag available + docs ready + oncall rotation knows how to pause a destination”. I don’t want us enabling for customers without the pause/degraded state.

Sean Gallagher: +100. Also: add an explicit alert threshold in beta: page if backlog_age > 30 min for >10 min OR success_rate < 98% for 15 min (per destination) AND destination is enabled.

Naomi Feldman: Cool. Action items:
- Naomi: finalize beta definition + success metrics doc + beta email blurb for CS (today EOD)
- Talia: build onboarding checklist + weekly feedback template (tomorrow)
- Colin/Fatima: confirm readiness + point-of-contact for Echelon + Stonewire, and whether they can do next week onboarding
- Sean: sanity check alert thresholds + what we can realistically measure in v0
- Marcus/Olga: review messaging on duplicates/PII and config-change audit trail

Colin O'Donnell: I’ll ping Echelon today. They wanted Datadog anyway. We should schedule 45 mins for “setup + test event + first query” and record any friction.

Fatima Noor: I’ll reach out to Stonewire CS contact. They also asked “can we filter to admin-only” which is a great test for include/exclude semantics.

Marcus Lin: Can you also add a question to weekly feedback: “Are you correlating these events with any other logs (API gateway / IAM)?” That impacts what fields we should treat as required for SIEM correlation.

Naomi Feldman: Yep. Adding.

Talia Benson: Also request for Sales/CS input (if you’re lurking): please reply here if there are other accounts we should prioritize OR any account we should avoid (e.g., procurement/security timeline that will bog down beta). We’ll keep the allowlist small (max 4) for first month.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: (also please don’t onboard 10 “friendly” customers at once; we will regret it)

Naomi Feldman: :thumbsup: Keeping it tight. I’ll post the finalized metrics + onboarding order back into this thread once updated.
